Note::TexAccessor::footnotes¶

Back to Note TeX Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

TokenBatch Note::TexAccessor::footnotes() const

Extract Footnote Bodies¶

footnotes() extracts the required brace argument of each exact \footnote control word. The command and braces are omitted; the authored body becomes the token. Both \footnote{body} and \footnote[mark]{body} are recognized, with the optional mark deliberately excluded because it controls numbering rather than note content.

Required arguments are parsed as balanced groups. A body such as {outer {nested} note} is therefore returned intact as outer {nested} note. Whitespace may separate the command, optional group, and required group. Longer command names such as \footnoted do not match, an escaped spelling does not match, and an unclosed optional or required group contributes no partial token. This is lexical extraction; macro expansion and TeX rendering are outside its contract.

Each receiver cell may contain a different number of notes, so the method returns TokenBatch. tokens() stores all bodies in lane and source order; offsets() maps them back to cells through half-open ranges. Duplicates and empty footnote bodies are retained because both are authored structures, not set members. Undefined input returns undefined tokens with offsets [0]. Defined non-Text Notes are rejected.

Scanning and balanced-group parsing are linear in the input bytes, plus the bytes copied into extracted bodies.

Example 1: Plain, Marked, And Nested Footnotes¶

const auto source = pluss::make_note({
    R"(Text\footnote{first} and \footnote[7]{outer {nested} note}.)",
    R"(\footnoted{not a footnote} \\footnote{escaped})",
    R"(\footnote{unfinished)"});
const auto notes = source.tex().footnotes();

std::cout << notes.tokens() << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[2], dim=1, numel=2, encoding=utf8)
["first", "outer {nested} note"]

The optional mark 7 is not content. The command-name prefix, escaped spelling, and malformed call are all ignored.

Example 2: Recover Lane Ownership¶

std::cout << "offsets=[";
const auto offsets = notes.offsets().integers();
for (std::size_t i = 0; i < offsets.size(); ++i)
  std::cout << (i ? ", " : "") << offsets[i];
std::cout << "]\n";

Output¶

offsets=[0, 2, 2, 2]

Both extracted bodies belong to cell zero. Cells one and two own empty ranges, rather than placeholder values.

Example 3: Undefined And Invalid Input¶

const auto absent = pluss::Note::undefined().tex().footnotes();
std::cout << std::boolalpha << absent.tokens().defined() << " offsets=["
          << absent.offsets().integers()[0] << "]\n";
try {
  (void)pluss::note::make(std::vector<std::int64_t>{1}).tex().footnotes();
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "footnotes Int64: rejected\n";
}

Output¶

false offsets=[0]
footnotes Int64: rejected
